summary: Two Blockers. The existing test test_subbox_sha.py case 3 asserts the old rule, and FR-5 leaves it out of the change set. The Math fixture of lines 36-60 cannot give empty feedback, because line 52 has no SHA. Six Majors and three Nits remain.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] spec.md FR-5 and plan.md Task 1.2: The existing test tests/spec_review_gate/test_subbox_sha.py::test_case_3_unticked_subbox_fails (lines 74-83) asserts one `plan task is not complete` line for an indented `[ ]` box under a SHA'd `[x]` parent. FR-1 makes that feedback empty, so the test fails after Green. FR-5 lists the change set as exactly five items and omits this test. Rationale: Task 1.2 names `bash tests/spec_review_gate/run.sh` as its suite, and the CI job `checks` runs it (.github/workflows/ci.yml:18), so the suite and Task 1.3 cannot pass; the spec leaves the edit of the old test (flip, rewrite, or delete) undecided.

F2 [Blocker] spec.md Acceptance Criteria and plan.md Task 1.1: The fixture "copied from Math plan lines 36-60" cannot give empty feedback. Line 52 of that plan is a top-level `[x]` without a SHA, and lines 53-60 are eight nested `[ ]` boxes under it. FR-1 gives one `completed plan task lacks commit SHA` line plus eight `plan task is not complete` lines. Only lines 38-50 (the task with a SHA) give empty feedback. Rationale: Red cannot write the case as specified, so Red must change the fixture or the rule, which is a decision the plan leaves to the implementer.
nonblocking_findings: F3 [Major] spec.md Overview: The text says every top-level task of the Math plan is `[x]` with a SHA. The file at that path has 25 top-level `[x]` lines (10 with a SHA), 4 top-level `[ ]` lines, and 1 top-level `[~]` line. Of the 226 nested `[ ]` lines, 215 sit under a top-level `[x]` without a SHA. A literal probe of FR-1 to FR-3 gives 291 feedback lines for that plan against 302 today, so the closeout check still fails for it. Rationale: the fix ignores 11 of the 226 nested lines of that plan; the spec premise is false for the file it names, and the Math failure is not fixed for that file.

F4 [Major] spec.md FR-3: The last sentence ("unless its own nearest shallower covered `[x]` parent covers it") conflicts with FR-1 ("the nearest `processed` entry with a smaller indent"). For a deeper box, the nearest entry is the ignored box itself. Reading 1 (nearest entry) leaves a `[x]` box without a SHA under an ignored `[ ]` box failing. Reading 2 (skip to the nearest covered `[x]`) covers it. FR-3 also does not state the stored tuple (status kept, covered False). Rationale: the two readings give different results for one input, and Red lists no case for it (F6), so an implementer can choose either and pass.

F5 [Major] spec.md FR-1 and FR-3: A `[ ]` box under an ignored `[ ]` box still fails. Probe: `- [x] T <sha>`, `  - [ ] s`, `    - [ ] ss` gives one `plan task is not complete` line for `ss`. Only the direct child of a covered `[x]` line is ignored. The title and Overview say closeout ignores nested sub-boxes, and the spec records no reason for the depth limit. Rationale: a three-level checklist under a covered task still blocks closeout, so the fix covers one form of the class. Across 1606 plans in the sibling repositories, the depth-1 rule and an any-depth rule gave the same result for each plan, so no data supports the limit. Record the reason, or ignore a `[ ]` or `[~]` box at any depth under a covered `[x]` ancestor.

F6 [Major] plan.md Task 1.1: The case list leaves rows of the input class and FR-3 untested. There is no case for a nested `[~]` box under a covered `[x]` parent, a `[ ]` box two levels under covered `[x]` boxes, a `[ ]` box under a `[~]` parent, a tab-indented sub-box, a `[ ]` box under an ignored `[ ]` box, or a `[x]` box under an ignored `[ ]` box. The case "a nested `[x]` box without a SHA under an uncovered parent" does not say whether the parent is a top-level `[ ]` or an ignored nested `[ ]`. The case "keeps today's feedback" does not name the message. Rationale: the task says it checks FR-1 through FR-4, but no case checks FR-3, and a Green that records an ignored box wrongly (F4) still passes the listed cases.

F7 [Major] spec.md FR-1 and FR-2: A parent line such as `- [x] Task (deferred)` is stored as `(indent, "x", True)`. FR-1 then ignores a nested `[ ]` box under it. Probe: today one `plan task is not complete` line, with FR-1 none. FR-2 says a nested box under a `deferred` parent keeps today's behaviour. Rationale: the two rules give opposite results for one input, the spec does not say which rule wins, and the plan names only a deferred `[ ]` parent.

F8 [Major] spec.md Acceptance Criteria and FR-2: The criterion "a nested `[ ]` box under an `[x]` parent without a SHA fails with `completed plan task lacks commit SHA`" names only the message of the parent. FR-1 does not ignore the box, so it also gets `plan task is not complete`. Probe: two lines for one parent and one box. Rationale: the expected feedback is not exact, so Red must choose between an exact list and a contains check; the eight boxes of Math lines 53-60 show that this is the common real form.

F9 [Nit] spec.md FR-0 and FR-4: FR-0 is a root-cause narrative, not a requirement. Both FRs cite line numbers (1093-1144, 1133, 431, 104) that move at each edit of the checker. Each number is correct at HEAD. Rationale: the symbol names keep the claims true after an edit and keep the spec at the requirement level.

F10 [Nit] plan.md Task 1.2 and spec.md FR-5: The plan names the CHANGELOG entry text but not its heading or form. Precedent entries sit under `## Unreleased` and `### Bug Fixes`, with a bold label, a sentence, and a `Track` id (CHANGELOG.md:47). The entry at CHANGELOG.md:47, the sentence at README.md:33, and the docstring of test_subbox_sha.py say that unticked boxes fail at every depth. Rationale: the format and placement change nothing in the checker; the old sentences drift from the new rule unless closeout updates them.

F11 [Nit] plan.md Task 1.1: Every case calls `plan_closeout_feedback` only, but the reported failure is the closeout check. Its callers `closeout_feedback` (measure_interphase_checks.py:1199) and `closeout_candidates` (line 464) change by design, and the spec does not say so. Rationale: one case through `closeout_candidates`, as in test_subbox_sha.py Class 2, proves that the check and the status list agree.

paraphrase.proposes: The track changes plan_closeout_feedback so an indented [ ] or [~] box gives no `plan task is not complete` feedback when its nearest shallower parent is a covered [x] line. Top-level open tasks, boxes under open or uncovered parents, and the SHA rule for [x] boxes keep today's behaviour. An ignored box is stored as not covered and never covers a deeper box. A new Red test and one CHANGELOG entry go in, and track_incomplete, phase_counts, and the jr-green branch stay unchanged.
paraphrase.current_system: plan_closeout_feedback reads every checkbox line and keeps (indent, status, covered) for each line. It appends `plan task is not complete` for each line that is not [x], at any depth, before the parent-cover rule runs. Per the spec, the Math plan has top-level [x] tasks with SHAs and 226 nested [ ] lines, so closeout fails. track_incomplete reads only column-0 lines, so it already ignores nested boxes. The closeout gate and the status candidate list both call plan_closeout_feedback.
